# -remote runs nvtop -x -record - on each host with ssh, and shows their
# devices in turn. A fake ssh stands in for the real one here: it plays
# the recording named for the host and stays connected.
[!exec:sh] skip
chmod 0755 bin/ssh
env PATH=$WORK${/}bin${:}$PATH

exec nvtop -x -remote alpha,beta -remote-cmd /opt/nvtop -d 5 -s
stdout '^   "host": "alpha",$'
stdout '^   "host": "beta",$'
stdout '"device_name": "NVIDIA GB10"'
stdout '"device_name": "NVIDIA H100"'
! stderr .
cmp args-alpha want-args

# A host that cannot be reached stops nvtop with ssh's complaint.
! exec nvtop -x -remote alpha,nowhere -s
stderr '^nvtop: nowhere: exit status 255: ssh: Could not resolve hostname nowhere$'

! exec nvtop -remote alpha -s
stderr '^nvtop: -remote needs -x$'
! exec nvtop -x -remote alpha,,beta -s
stderr 'host names separated by commas'
! exec nvtop -x -remote-cmd nvtop -s
stderr '^nvtop: -remote-cmd needs -remote$'

-- bin/ssh --
#!/bin/sh
# ssh -T -o BatchMode=yes HOST COMMAND
host=$4
dir=$(dirname "$0")/..
echo "$@" > "$dir/args-$host"
if [ ! -f "$dir/$host.jsonl" ]; then
	echo "ssh: Could not resolve hostname $host" >&2
	exit 255
fi
cat "$dir/$host.jsonl"
exec sleep 30
-- want-args --
-T -o BatchMode=yes alpha /opt/nvtop -x -record - -d 5
-- alpha.jsonl --
{"time":"2026-09-25T10:00:00Z","devices":[{"name":"NVIDIA GB10","gpu_util":3,"mem_total":130662940672,"mem_used":18993635328}]}
-- beta.jsonl --
{"time":"2026-09-25T10:00:00Z","devices":[{"name":"NVIDIA H100","gpu_util":90,"temp_c":70},{"name":"NVIDIA H100","gpu_util":0}]}
